Header:
Date: 2025-12-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jamal White (Redwood Solutions), Priya Nair (Sapphire Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Sapphire Infra Lead), Maya Patel (Sapphire Security), Oliver Grant (Sapphire Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Sapphire is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive recommender and chat features. Primary concerns: isolation, committed GPU capacity, predictable throughput, burst strategy, and audit/compliance. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing + security docs, run a 1-week benchmark using Sapphire sample traffic, and reconvene to finalize PoC scoping.

Topics: dedicated capacity, reserved GPUs, VPC/private deployment, burst capacity, autoscale policies, quantization and performance tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS/audit logs, rollback and rollouts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off — this is alyssa from redwood, with marco our se and jamal on solutions. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya: good, thanks. excited to dig in, we've been looking at hosted options but our SREs flagged isolation and predictable throughput as must-haves.
[00:12] Ethan: yeah we run recommender + a chat assistant, mean latencies need to be <200ms p95 for short prompts, and we also have heavy batch embedding jobs overnight.
[00:20] Marco: gotcha, so for those patterns Dedicated is usually what customers pick — reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, plus burst options for spiky traffic. quick q, what's your target commit window? monthly, annual?
[00:30] Priya: prefer annual but want ability to burst beyond baseline without crazy egress costs.
[00:35] Oliver: and for security we need VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS, plus RBAC and audit logs. our legal team will want retention controls.
[00:42] Jamal: that aligns with what Redwood Private can do; Dedicated is a middle ground — reserved hardware but still managed by redwood. we support private deployments too if you want the whole control plane in your VPC.
[00:52] Maya: clarify that — if we pick Dedicated, is data ever leaving our network? we need to understand encryption at rest/in transit and key ownership.
[01:00] Marco: with Dedicated you get network isolation from other tenants, and we can integrate with your KMS for key ownership. data-in-transit is TLS, at rest is encrypted — we also export audit events to your SIEM. i'll send the security pack.
[01:15] Priya: perfect. on capacity sizing, i want to understand how you model reserved GPUs vs burst. do you use autoscaling across node pools or queueing?
[01:25] Marco: good q. we offer reserved GPU pools sized by committed vGPU count. there's autoscaling for worker pools and an optional burst tier that uses shared capacity at a lower priority. bursts are first-fit but we surface fallback policies — e.g., route to a lighter quantized model or to hosted fallback.
[01:40] Ethan: how deterministic is the latency when bursting? our SLAs expect consistent p95.
[01:45] Marco: bursts are best-effort, so latency can vary. we recommend keeping baseline capacity at ~70-80% of expected sustained QPS for latency-sensitive paths, and using burst for rare spikes; also you can configure an always-on canary instance to absorb small spikes.
[01:58] Priya: ok makes sense. what about model variants — can we pin different quantization profiles for canary vs stable?
[02:05] Marco: yes, you can pin model versions and quantization profiles per route. you can do canary rollouts or traffic-splits for A/B tests. model artifacts are versioned in the catalog.
[02:15] Oliver: curious about batching and KV cache — does redwood manage KV cache across requests to reduce latency for chat-like workloads?
[02:23] Marco: we do continuous batching and KV cache management built into the runtime. for chat with long contexts we keep per-session KV caches to avoid reencoding. for embeddings we batch aggressively during off-peak.
[02:33] Ethan: any guidance on GPU types for our workloads? we have long context generation and some heavy transformer cross-attention work.
[02:40] Marco: depends on model size and quantization. for 70B-ish models you'd want A100/TrnX equivalent; for quantized 8-bit variants you can run on smaller nodes. we'll run a sizing exercise during the PoC to recommend exact instance types and counts.
[02:55] Priya: benchmark — we want a 1-week perf run with our sample traffic. can you outline what you need from us?
[03:00] Marco: we'll need sample prompts, traffic distribution, expected QPS, and a scrubbed dataset for embeddings. also whether you want end-to-end latencies including network hop or just inference time.
[03:12] Priya: end-to-end please. we want to ensure realistic numbers.
[03:16] Jamal: noted. maya, any security items you want raised now?
[03:20] Maya: SOC2 is required, we use SAML SSO, need role-based access controls, and specific retention windows for logs. also interested in where the audit logs live and whether redwood can forward to our SIEM.
[03:29] Marco: we support SAML/SSO and granular RBAC; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or stored in your VPC. our security pack includes SOC2 report and our pen test summary.
[03:38] Maya: good. question on key management: can you support customer-managed keys in HSM?
[03:43] Jamal: yes we integrate with cloud KMS/HSM providers for customer-managed keys. for private deployments we can also integrate with customer HSM on-prem.
[03:50] Ethan: on cost — what's the billing model for Dedicated? flat reserved + usage for bursts?
[03:55] Alyssa: typically it's a committed monthly fee for reserved capacity and an overage rate for bursts or excess usage. pricing varies with GPU class and commitment length; i'll include tiered pricing in the doc we send.
[04:06] Priya: do you offer autoscaling policies that scale down safely without wiping model warm state? we want to avoid cold-start penalty.
[04:13] Marco: we have warm pools and smart scale-down that prefer idled workers to be kept warm based on predicted traffic; you can also configure minimum warm instances per route. that reduces cold-starts.
[04:23] Oliver: what's the expected lead time to spin up Dedicated capacity for an annual commitment?
[04:28] Alyssa: depends on capacity availability and region — typically 2-6 weeks for provisioning and validation; private deployments longer. we'll surface exact timelines in the proposal.
[04:36] Ethan: for the PoC, can we test both hosted fallback and dedicated-only to compare latency/cost?
[04:41] Marco: yes we can set up a split traffic scenario — some percentage to Dedicated, some to hosted, and measure delta. that'll show the economics and tail latency differences.
[04:50] Priya: any limitations on model size for Dedicated? we have mixed model family needs including open-source Llama-style and some custom fine-tuned models.
[04:58] Marco: we support a broad model catalog and onboarding custom weights; model size is bounded by available GPU memory and shard strategy. we'll validate during onboarding.
[05:06] Maya: compliance question: can you provide logs demonstrating data access for audits?
[05:10] Jamal: yes audit logs include access events and admin actions, and we can provide long-term retention options.
[05:16] Priya: curious about fallback quality — if we route to a quantized variant during burst, do you see significant quality regressions?
[05:23] Marco: depends on model and task; for many generation tasks 4-bit/8-bit quantized models produce acceptable quality, but for sensitive tasks we recommend A/B evals on your prompts. Redwood Optimize helps suggest quantization profiles by workload.
[05:36] Oliver: what's the typical unit economics difference between Hosted and Dedicated for us?
[05:41] Alyssa: Dedicated tends to lower per-token cost at scale because of reserved capacity and better batching; Hosted is cheaper to start with but can be more expensive at high sustained QPS. we'll include a cost model spreadsheet.
[05:52] Priya: timeline — we want to run the benchmark next week and have a proposal by the following week if numbers look good.
[05:58] Alyssa: sounds good. to recap, we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark runbook. marco will run the perf tests with you, and we'll reconvene to agree on PoC scope.
[06:09] Priya: cool, thanks everyone.
[06:12] Alyssa: thanks, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
